title: The Envy of Hyle and the Five Living Fires
description: T74 names envy as the very first motion of the proprium — the original shape of self-love in the natural mind, the seed-form of every later wickedness. When the divine humanity goes forth, the proprium sees the image, cannot bear that it should not be its own, and spits venom on the outer truth. It envies the call's icon and stamps a counterfeit upon its flesh; envies the formed man and snatches what was given; envies all the first works — every good the Lord brings forth, the proprium tries to penetrate with its claim. T75 sets against this the eight dwellings of living love: in the natural mind as ground, in the Father at his inmost, in the Divine Human as armor, in the vessel of the day as illumining wisdom, in the vessel of the night as receivable wisdom, in the call going out, in the new land as pure receivability, in the visible signs sun and moon — divine love at every register from natural ground to visible cosmic sign.
